The devs at Arrowhead are genuinely amazing and dedicated to their community. But I decided to have an actual review of what I can say.

The game has one of the most healthy monetization set ups. The game has a 'warbond' system, you start with a free one unlocked that should give you enough currency to unlock one other warbond. After that grinding it and unlocking the last couple you can get from other warbonds will be how you get them. Warbonds are basically battlepasses, except they last forever and don't require real money.

If you suffer from the fear of missing out, this game pushes that to the side. Every 2 days 2 sets of armors are in the premium store, and they aren't too hard to grind enough to buy them, but their stats and bonuses are typically the same as any armor you could get in a battle pass. With so far two traits being ONLY for warbond armor. And the armor will certainly come back as it's on rotation. There has not once been armor that you had to buy now or you'd never get a chance. With exception to the pre-order sets, which 1 of the 3 sets does have a unique model, but the rest are recolors of armor you can already get.

The only other time limited item besides that was a free cape for fighting on a certain planet.

I'll let other reviews talk about other aspects of the game, but if you have unhealthy spending habits or low self control, Helldivers won't exploit you and milk every drop of cash they can get.
You'll only have FOMO when it comes to exterminating bugs.

Sony got a taste of that Liber-TEA. MMMMMM. I was so worried for this game with the backlash it was receiving on account linking, thinking Sony just killed one of the best things it had going for it. But they backpedaled and I am so grateful. Kudos to the community for affecting one hell of a change.

Corporate Justice aside, this game has one of the best content and risk/reward structures I've seen.

- Nothing is "forcing you" to pay actual money to unlock additional content. You play the game, you can find currency spread out in the world. Run enough missions and you will have all the Super Credits you need to unlock upcoming warbonds, and then some.

- Play harder difficulties to increase your reward chances. I'll tell you what, Helldiver difficutly kicked my squad's ASS for the the longest time. And at times, it still does. But the feeling of extracting with all those samples..one step closer to unlocking all those ship upgrades...it's SO satisfying.

Overall, the game is a breath of fresh air in the shooters category. I was hesitant at first, but after a taste I'm all in. Thanks Arrowhead.

I loved this game. Pure and Joyous democracy spread across the galaxy with your friends. The variety of weapons and stratagems the game offers is one of its big selling points. You get to customize your loadout to suit a playstyle or to handle specific threats you know will be present. The stratagem call in system is simple and easy to understand, yet so perfectly challenging in the heat of combat. The gun play is clean and almost every weapon feels powerful in a suitable situation.

With each successful mission you are shown your contribution and, as an individual, it feels good to see that liberation percent tick up. You can also see the liberation percent increase other players complete their own missions. It really makes you feel part of a bigger picture. You are making progress and you aren't alone in doing it. With every planet liberated a narrative is forming behind the scenes.. being written by our actions. Its so awesome to be able to see it unfold over time and know that you helped shape that outcome.

All that being said, I cannot recommend this game right now. 

Every patch brings new "balance" changes that will take a weapon and nerf/change or or buff enemies so the way you used to deal with them just doesn't work anymore. On top of that, the game is currently plagued with bugs. Crashes, disconnects and desync ruin many games. Even some egregious issues like non functioning cover and phantom hitboxes that can launch you off the map if you brush up against them. 

All the while new content gets pumped out for the game in the form of warbonds that can be purchased with real money. But why would I be interested in buying them if half the new content might not even work? maybe its because the weapon I did enjoy using just doesn't feel fun anymore because the developers decided to change it.

Helldivers 2 is one of the best games to release so far this year. Its just a shame that every update that comes out feels like it takes some of the fun away. I want to love this game like I did when it first launched. Maybe I will once Arrowhead finally gets their priorities straightened out.

WE DEFEATED SONY!!!! FOR DEMOCRACY!!!

A game that is community driven, responsive to community input, and is fun and challenging as hell?

Hell yeah.

You know what I love? A game that's funny. A game with funny dialogue, funny player choices and the freedom to do funny things to other players without consequence and boy howdy does Helldivers II deliver on the humour.

If Sony's insidious 3rd party software turned you off from this in mid 2024, they amended all that.

It is the most fun PVE shooting/action game. If they can squeeze in some Titanfall-style mech gameplay then this game would be perfect, PERFECT!!!
Now it's not as if it isn't perfect in its own way. Helldivers 2 offers extremely agile, acrobatic 3D Movement by the player. Controls are most similar to Metal Gear Solid GZ/V. Sprinting, leaping into a prone position and with great rewards for intelligent use of stealth.

Weapons, this game has dozens of them. Some better than others but all of them fill a niche. I'm a big fan of the HALT shotgun, because if you have a buddy and you're using the stun shells it makes most medium-heavy enemies trivial. No more Berserker swarms or Alpha Commander pajama parties. 

The variety of enemy forces caters to multiple PVE styles. You have careful tactical shooter gameplay against the Automatons, you have swarm gameplay requiring dextrous movement and ample use of shrapnel explosives with the Terminids, and now you have knuckle-paleing urban combat against those repulsive squid cretins, the Illuminate. 

You want to carpet bomb a city? You can do that. HE, Toxic Gas, Napalm.
You want to drop a nuclear bomb on a small creature? Buddy, you've got 2 nukes to excrete upon whatever lifeform you want once you upgrade your nukes.
You want to kill a 40K Dreadnought style robot with a single revolver round? You can do that IF YOU PRACTICE, HOT SHOT!

You want to sprint around like Terry Fox with a bum leg spreading positive vibes* to the various alien races? You can have up to 5 damaged limbs in this game at once. There's even an achievement for that, I don't have it yet I think I need a specific armour set.
 
You want to host a game and execute your teammates for cowardice/incompetence/no reason? There is literally no penalty to doing so. You can kill your teammates, with such variety, you can dedicate your first 20 hours to learning how to make doing so look like an accident.

Most importantly, you want to have FUN? You want to laugh, hold your belly like Santa Claus and chortle into the microphone with some music I can't stand creeping in over the mic? Friend, you can do it.

Buy this game, play it with me. Nuke me, drop a tesla coil on me, gas me, sass me, embrace me as the fireball consumes us. Play however you like. 

There is nothing like Helldivers 2.
